page.layout: One printed page (p. 319). Top: one column of running text, continued from the previous page. Below a rule: centred title block (division head, subtitle, "Theses Pontificiae" line), then one italic thesis paragraph with its citation. Bottom: signature at left, catchword at right. The narrow strip at the far left is the edge of the neighbouring page and is not transcribed.

main_text.p: nos, imo jam probasse confidimus, Ecclesiam illam, quam unicam Jesuitæ probant, & venerantur, cuius Caput est Romanus Pontifex, cuius membra sunt homines sine ulla interna virtute, cuius regula non sit regula fidei in solis Scripturis tradita, sed Romanæ traditiones non scriptæ: non esse Ecclesiam illam unicam, quam suo sanguine redemit Christus, quam instituerunt Apostoli, quam retinuerunt Patres, quæ victrix contra mundum, & Antichristum, contra vitia & hæreses ad finem usque mundi est duratura, & in æternum cum Christo regnatura: sed esse synagogam ab Ecclesia diversam, quæ nec antiquitatem ante exortos fraterculorum ordines, nec auctoritatem ante Concilii Tridentini tempora ostendere possit.
main_text.head: TERTIA CONTROVERSIA. DE FIDE IUSTIFICANTE.
THESES PONTIFICIÆ.
main_text.p: Si quis dixerit, sola fide impium iustificari, ut intelligat nihil aliud requiri, quod ad iustificationis gratiam consequendam cooperetur, & nulla ex parte necesse esse, cum sua voluntatis motu[?] præparari, atque disponi, anathema sit. Concil. Trident. sessio. 6. can.9.

page.notes: The page header and the text in the upper column are clear; the first line is a fragment carried over from the previous page. Doubtful readings: "motu" in the thesis (blurred, could be "mota" or similar), and the comma after "iustificari" (partly obscured by a dark stain). The lower part of the page is heavily stained and blurred, so the thesis wording has been checked only where the letters can be seen. The stain at the lower centre and the show-through of the reverse side have been left out. The bottom-right catchword "Si" is partly cut off by the edge of the page and may be incomplete.
